Adjusted Similarity Between Two Feature Sets

Source: R/metrics.R
adjusted_similarity.Rd

Computes a chance-corrected similarity between two feature sets. Unlike jaccard_similarity(), the adjusted measure accounts for the expected random overlap given the sizes of both sets and the total feature universe, so it does not systematically penalise methods that select many features.

Usage

adjusted_similarity(
  set1 = NULL,
  set2 = NULL,
  n_universe = NULL,
  list1 = NULL,
  list2 = NULL,
  nb_total_elements = NULL
)

Arguments

set1

Character or integer vector of selected feature identifiers.

set2

Character or integer vector of selected feature identifiers.

n_universe

Integer; total number of candidate features in the universe (i.e. the number of columns in the original predictor matrix).

list1

Deprecated; use set1 instead. If supplied by name, a deprecation warning is emitted and the value is used as set1 when the latter is NULL. It will be removed in a future release.

list2

Deprecated; use set2 instead. If supplied by name, a deprecation warning is emitted and the value is used as set2 when the latter is NULL. It will be removed in a future release.

nb_total_elements

Deprecated; use n_universe instead. If supplied by name, a deprecation warning is emitted and the value is used as n_universe when the latter is NULL. It will be removed in a future release.

Value

Numeric scalar in \((-1, 1]\). Values above 0 indicate more overlap than expected by chance; 1 means perfect agreement; negative values indicate less overlap than chance.

Details

The formula is analogous to Cohen's kappa for sets: $$S_{\text{adj}}(A, B) = \frac{r - \mathbb{E}[r]}{\min(k_1, k_2) - \max(0, k_1 + k_2 - d)}$$ where \(r = |A \cap B|\), \(k_i = |A_i|\), \(d =\) n_universe, and \(\mathbb{E}[r] = k_1 k_2 / d\).

Returns 0 when either set is empty or equals the full universe (edge cases where the correction denominator is zero).

See also

adjusted_similarity_pairwise() for computing all pairwise values at once, adjusted_similarity_summary() for a summary statistic, jaccard_similarity() for the non-chance-corrected alternative.

Examples

# 10-feature universe; sets A and B share 2 out of 3 features each
adjusted_similarity(c("f1","f2","f3"), c("f2","f3","f4"), n_universe = 10L)
#> [1] 0.3666667
adjusted_similarity(c("f1","f2"),      c("f1","f2"),      n_universe = 10L) # 0.8
#> [1] 0.8
adjusted_similarity(character(0),      c("f1"),           n_universe = 10L) # 0
#> [1] 0
